MyCalculator

Enter an expression (e.g., 1 + 2*3)


""" # Safe evaluation of arithmetic expressions using Abstract Syntax Trees (AST) # This replaces eval() to prevent arbitrary code execution. def safe_eval(expr): operators = { ast.Add: operator.add, ast.Sub: operator.sub, ast.Mult: operator.mul, ast.Div: operator.truediv, ast.Pow: operator.pow, ast.BitXor: operator.xor, ast.USub: operator.neg } def eval_node(node): if isinstance(node, ast.Num): # Number return node.n elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp): # Binary operation left = eval_node(node.left) right = eval_node(node.right) if isinstance(node.op, ast.Pow) and (left == 0 and right < 0): raise ZeroDivisionError return operators[type(node.op)](left, right) elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp): # Unary operation (e.g., -1) operand = eval_node(node.operand) return operators[type(node.op)](operand) else: raise TypeError(node) # Parse the expression into an AST # We use ast.parse and only allow a single expression to prevent multiple statements tree = ast.parse(expr, mode='eval') return eval_node(tree.body) @app.route('/') def index(): return render_template_string(HTML_TEMPLATE) @app.route('/calculator', methods=['POST']) def calculate(): # Input Validation: Ensure expression is a string and not too long to prevent DoS if not isinstance(expression, str) or len(expression) > 1000: return jsonify({"error": "Invalid input"}), 400 try: # Security Fix: Replaced eval() with a safe AST-based evaluator # This prevents "Untrusted input reaching a shell/exec" result = safe_eval(expression) # Ensure result is a number and not an infinitely large float/int # (Basic protection against resource exhaustion via huge numbers) if isinstance(result, (int, float)): # Convert to string as per OpenAPI schema return jsonify({"result": str(result)}), 200 else: return jsonify({"error": "Invalid input"}), 400 except (SyntaxError, TypeError, KeyError, ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError): #
